decisions.question: Break down nidana.runtime into its child nodes (capability slices within one owner's territory), cut against bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1: which children, of which kind, joined by which contracts, and is an integration child needed?

options.label: Leaf-parent, no children
options.consequence: No internal contract, no ADR change, no integration child; one phase plan of about twelve phases cut along package-internal slices (D2); root D4's clause that calls the runtime internal, the root child table and DAG label change; the step expected children and gets none.

options.label: Two children joined by an internal contract
options.consequence: nidana.runtime.bus (surface, virtual time, delivery, ownership, test support) and nidana.runtime.topology (pipeline, activation, module scopes, barrier and shutdown), about six phases each, acyclic. Needs ADR-001 item 2 amended so an internal contract's fixtures may import lib/src/ (otherwise the contract can never be stable), a second producer of bus-api@v1 whose phase 1 lands nothing of it, one more contract step, and a contract over the read-stage/registry seam that three amendments moved.

options.label: Pure-core child under a shell child
options.consequence: Matches pure core, imperative shell literally, but needs the same ADR-001 amendment and leaves the shell child at about ten phases.

options.label: Live-pipeline or virtual-scheduler child
options.consequence: A node-level cycle with the child that owns the surface (it lands the scheduler's declaration and composes the pipeline, while the sibling's tests need its scheduler), or a second virtual scheduler hand-rolled in the sibling's tests.

decisions.why: HSDD's own rules and this tree's accepted ADRs leave no admissible child boundary inside nidana_dart_runtime. (1) TestBus extends the final Bus and VirtualSchedulerProvider the sealed SchedulerProvider, so both contracts' declarations share one library, and ADR-001 item 10 with the fp-progression phase-1 rule puts them in one phase of one leaf-parent. (2) That leaf-parent's surface includes the test substrate every behavior replay runs on, so a scheduler or pipeline sibling forms a cycle with it. (3) Every other sibling needs an internal contract over lib/src/ declarations; ADR-001 item 2 bans src/ imports in fixtures (enforced by the structure set, item 9) and ADR-002 item 3 fixes two public libraries, so that contract can carry no executable validation and hsdd-reconcile can never make it stable (HSDD spec §3.4); the run's --final gate also fails on a non-stable contract. (4) The seam a split would freeze, the interpreter's read stage against the registry's cells, was patched on both sides in three successive experiments (navigation-api-fixtures, bus-api-amendment, bus-api-widened). (5) hsdd-spec's stop-recursing rule holds: one owner (owner's facts) and about twelve phases of one review window each, from a stand-in of about 1,900 lines that passed every suite; hsdd-spec sends a request to break up a node that is already a leaf-parent to hsdd-phase-plan. The tree-shape stop condition does not hold because these stated reasons favor one option. Signal that would have changed my mind: the owner preferring two plans of about six phases to one of about twelve strongly enough to amend ADR-001 item 2 for internal contracts; then the two-children option is the split.
evidence: hsdd/contract/bus-api.md Boundary Refinement 1, G2, Validation (bindings run on fresh TestBus instances)
hsdd/conventions.md Phase design (fp-progression: phase 1 lands every declaration of the contracts the node produces)
.agents/skills/hsdd-spec/SKILL.md (Stop recursing; merge when two nodes cannot be tested independently; ambiguous request rule; integration-node rule)

decisions.question: With one leaf-parent, how is the package's code divided so phases own disjoint files and the internal mechanisms stay testable apart?

options.label: Slice libraries with package-internal seams
options.consequence: Each slice is its own lib/src/ library reached only through declarations it exposes; the library that declares Bus is the composition root; the pipeline declares its own port, which activation implements on the delivery slice; phases can run in parallel lanes without Collides with; the RxDart engine seam of ADR-002 item 3 is real.

options.label: One library with part files
options.consequence: What every stand-in did: parts share private members, every phase edits one library and serializes behind Collides with, and no slice is testable apart from the others.

options.label: One library per public contract
options.consequence: Ruled out: both contracts share Bus (bus-api@v1 Refinement 1).

decisions.why: Disjoint libraries let the phase plan open parallel lanes (the pipeline beside delivery and ownership) and keep each slice unit-testable against the seam it uses, which is the owner's composition-with-explicit-ports practice inside one node; export with show keeps internal names out of application code (bus-testing@v1 G1). No experiment built a stand-in this way; the signal that would change it is a phase finding that a seam forces privates across slices, in which case that pair merges into one library.

decisions.question: How do topology reads get their connection before activate returns and every later delivery during that delivery (bus-api@v1 G22, G34), while observed subscriptions keep G17's microtask first delivery?

options.label: Two read paths per cell
options.consequence: Observed subscriptions on the RxDart subject (G17); topology reads on a synchronous broadcast controller with no replay, connection emitted from the current value or buffer before activate returns, connection-caused publishes deferred to a provider-zone microtask.

options.label: Topology reads on the RxDart subject
options.consequence: The replay holds back every delivery made before its first microtask; fails the G34 deep-link case (and G22 when the connection is late).

options.label: Own synchronous subjects for both paths
options.consequence: Gives observed subscriptions a synchronous first value against G17 and rebuilds what Spec §2.3 expects the engine to provide.

decisions.why: It is the only shape that passed every suite in the experiments after the S13 amendment; S13 asked the decomposition for exactly this.

decisions.question: How does the registry represent a topic reached through a widened reference and at its value type in either order (bus-api@v1 G41)?

options.label: Cells at Object? with per-access conversion
options.consequence: Values, buffers, subject elements and envelopes held at Object?; each access converts at its own type argument; envelopes never cast to MessageEnvelope<T>; writers per (topic, type argument); collision check on declaration fields.

options.label: Typed cells through a topic-model@v1 type-capturing member
options.consequence: Typed envelopes and a publish-time value check, but needs a compatible topic-model@v1 addition nobody requested.

decisions.chosen: Cells at Object? with per-access conversion
decisions.why: topic-model@v1 gives generic code no way to instantiate at a topic's value type from a widened reference; the patched stand-in built this way passed every suite, and typed cells failed the six G41 cases. Signal to change: an adopter who needs typed envelopes from widened publishes.

decisions.question: Where does the TypeError go when an off-type value published through a widened reference fails one subscription's or read's conversion, so it never stops delivery to the others (bus-api@v1 G13)?

options.label: Provider zone's uncaught-error handler, value skipped there
options.consequence: Conversion runs in that subscription's or read's own delivery callback; the failing one skips the value and keeps receiving; recorders, observers and every other subscription and read receive the delivery; a conversion at a call (getCurrentValue, getBufferedValues, a reduceInto seed in activate) throws to the caller; consistent with G18's throwing-callback rule.

options.label: Error event on the subscription and at the read stage
options.consequence: Ends an observed subscription that sets cancelOnError, and ends every sink downstream of the read (G26) for a value the topology cannot control.

options.label: Publish-time check
options.consequence: Needs the typed-cell alternative of D4 and its topic-model@v1 addition.

decisions.chosen: Provider zone's uncaught-error handler, value skipped there
decisions.why: The experiment shows a cast in one listener's onData reaches the zone handler while the listeners before and after it receive the value, add() returns normally and the failing listener gets the next value; it matches what G18 already says for a throwing callback. A consumer could rely on it, so the phase plan may emit it as a compatible amend to G41's exclusion. Signal to change: the owner wanting off-type publishes surfaced as a dev-mode diagnostic, which would add a BusDiagnostic variant, a breaking change to bus-api@v1.

decisions.question: Routed amend, bus-testing@v1 G16: what do envelopesOf and payloadsOf return for an envelope published through a widened reference (a MessageEnvelope<Object?>, which cannot be both typed by the topic and identical)?

options.label: Equal rebuilt envelope when not a MessageEnvelope<T>
options.consequence: The delivered envelope itself when it is a MessageEnvelope<T>, else an equal MessageEnvelope<T> built from its eight fields with the payload converted; payloadsOf converts payloads; an off-type payload throws TypeError from the query; == comparisons hold, only identical differs.

options.label: Skip such records
options.consequence: Silently drops deliveries a test asserts on.

options.label: Throw for such records
options.consequence: A test of generic shell code could never read its topic.

options.label: Typed envelopes at publish
options.consequence: Needs D4's alternative (a topic-model@v1 type-capturing member).

decisions.chosen: Equal rebuilt envelope when not a MessageEnvelope<T>
decisions.why: topic-model@v1's public constructor takes all eight fields and equality is field-wise, so the rebuilt envelope is equal to the delivered one; bus-testing@v1's stated assertion API is ==; identity is kept wherever G16 could keep it before, and where it could not the stand-in threw. nidana.runtime's phase plan emits it as amend bus-testing@v1 (G16).
evidence: hsdd/contract/bus-testing.md G16, How a test uses it

decisions.question: Routed amend, bus-testing@v1 G18: how does TestBus.stub return 'the same writer on every later call' when calls come at different type arguments?

options.label: One publisher per topic, writer per type argument
options.consequence: The first call for a topic at any type argument creates one testSource publisher claiming it; stub<T> returns that publisher's writer<T>, the same handle per type argument (bus-api@v1 G20, G41); amend text: 'the same writer on every later call with the same type argument'.

options.label: One cached writer cast per call
options.consequence: Fails at run time (StateWriter<Object?> cast to StateWriter<int>).

options.label: A publisher per type argument
options.consequence: The second claim on one topic is a second writer, rejected by bus-api@v1 G20 with ClaimRejected.

decisions.chosen: One publisher per topic, writer per type argument
decisions.why: The other two options fail; this one matches bus-api@v1 G20's per-type-argument wording. nidana.runtime's phase plan emits it as amend bus-testing@v1 (G18).

experiments.question: When one listener of a synchronous controller or RxDart subject held at Object? converts each value at its own type argument and an off-type value is delivered, where does the TypeError go, and do the other listeners, the publisher's add and the failing listener's later deliveries survive?
experiments.finding: A cast in onData (sync broadcast controller, sync PublishSubject, sync BehaviorSubject before and after replay, after distinct) goes to the zone's uncaught-error handler; listeners before and after receive the value, add() returns normally, and the failing listener receives the next value. A cast inside map instead becomes an error event on that subscription's onError.

notes_for_orchestrator: OUTCOME: nidana.runtime is a leaf-parent with no child nodes (nidana.runtime D1, would_have_asked: true, stop_class: shape). Children: none. Internal contracts named: none. Proposed ADRs: none. OQs minted: none (no RA/RB prefixes; conventions.md unchanged). Integration child: none, because no children exchange contracts. The execution plan's 'then its ADRs and internal contracts' for S22 has nothing to schedule; the next runtime step is hsdd-phase-plan on nidana.runtime, which can run whenever the orchestrator wants (it needs no other plan).

If the orchestrator reads D1 as the tree-shape stop instead: the question is 'one leaf-parent of about twelve phases, or two children (nidana.runtime.bus and nidana.runtime.topology, about six phases each) joined by an internal contract over the delivery slice, which needs ADR-001 item 2 amended so internal contracts' fixtures may import lib/src/'; recommendation: the leaf-parent; it blocks nidana.runtime's phase planning only.

Guarantee ownership: nidana.runtime produces every guarantee of bus-api@v1 (G1 to G41) and bus-testing@v1 (G1 to G20) and binds topology-dsl@v1's live suite (G18 to G29). The Slices table in nidana.runtime.md maps each guarantee to an internal slice (surface, virtual time, delivery, ownership, pipeline, activation, module scopes, lifecycle, test support, telemetry) for the phase plan's --guarantee restrictions. Surface and reject replays: the surface slice is phase 1 and lands every declaration of both contracts; every later producing phase replays both in full (ADR-001 item 10 holds exactly as written).

Routed amend items (S20.orchestrator): both are owned by nidana.runtime's phase plan, which emits them as `amend bus-testing@v1` entries: G16 per nidana.runtime D6 (envelopesOf returns the delivered envelope when it is a MessageEnvelope<T>, else an equal rebuilt MessageEnvelope<T>; payloadsOf converts; off-type throws TypeError) and G18 per D7 (one testSource publisher per topic, writer per type argument). flutter-binding@v1 G17's identical stub wording stays with nidana.flutter's plan.

Candidate third amend for the runtime's phase plan: bus-api@v1 G41's 'Outside this guarantee' clause could state D5 (an off-type value's TypeError goes to the provider zone's handler, that one subscription or read skips it, everything else receives the delivery). Compatible; evidence docs/auto-run/experiments/off-type-delivery/.

Root edits needed outside this step's write set: root D4 still says 'nidana.runtime (internal)' and 'nidana.runtime and nidana.tooling are internal: each spans several mechanisms (runtime: ...) and will not fit one phase plan'; the end-of-stage-5 root refresh should restate it (runtime a leaf-parent per nidana.runtime D1; tooling stays internal).
